'''Dehradun Airport''' {{Airport codes|DED|VIDN}}, also known as '''Jolly Grant Airport''', is a [[domestic airport]] serving [[Dehradun]], the capital of [[Uttarakhand]], [[India]]. It is located in Jauligrant, {{convert|25|km|mi|abbr=on}} south of the city, {{convert|20|km|mi|abbr=on}} from [[Rishikesh]] and {{convert|35|km|mi|abbr=on}} from [[Haridwar]]. Commercial operations began on 30 March 2008, after the runway was extended to accommodate larger aircraft. A new terminal building was inaugurated in February 2009.<ref name="PIB">{{cite web |title=New Integrated Terminal Buildings inaugurated at Amritsar, Dehradun and Jaipur Airport |url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=47938 |access-date=7 August 2014 |newspaper=[[Press Information Bureau]] |date=25 February 2009}}</ref> The current passenger terminal was inaugurated in October 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 October 2021 |first=Kautilya |last=Singh |title=U'khand gets new airport terminal bldg, heli services for seven routes flagged off |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/dehradun/ukhand-gets-new-airport-terminal-bldg-heli-services-for-seven-routes-flagged-off/articleshow/86876188.cms |access-date=8 July 2022 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref> The airport is the [[List of the busiest airports in India|32nd-busiest airport in India]], with over 1.5 million annual passengers.

It is also known as the ''Air Gateway of Garhwal'' and plays an important role in the [[Tourism in Uttarakhand|tourism of Uttarakhand]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Pandit |first=Ambika |title=Dehradun airport sees flurry of action |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Dehradun-airport-sees-flurry-of-action/articleshow/20771587.cms |access-date=26 June 2013 |newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |date=26 June 2013}}</ref>

==History==
The airport was constructed in 1974.<ref name= "PFR">{{cite web |title=PRE-FEASIBILITY REPORT (PFR) FOR OBTAINING TOR FOR EXPANSION OF DEHRADUN AIRPORT |url=http://environmentclearance.nic.in/writereaddata/Online/TOR/09_Oct_2017_205826423QT0Q3Y2MPFR.pdf |access-date=24 September 2020 |publisher=[[Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change]] }}</ref> [[Vayudoot]] operated scheduled services to [[New Delhi]], [[Lucknow]] and [[Pantnagar]] from 1982 to 1995.<ref name="TRB">{{cite news |title=Aviation giants land at Jolly Grant airport |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/2010/20100330/dun.htm#1 |access-date=7 August 2014 |newspaper=[[The Tribune (Chandigarh)|The Tribune]] |date=28 March 2008}}</ref> [[Air Deccan]] started flights between Dehradun and [[New Delhi]] in December 2004,<ref>{{cite news |title=Air Deccan to fly Delhi-Dehradun |url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2004/dec/21deccan1.html |access-date=7 August 2014 |work=[[Rediff.com]] |date=21 December 2004}}</ref> and added a second daily flight from August 2006.<ref>{{cite news |title=Air Deccan launches 2 flight on Delhi-Dehradun-Delhi sector |url=http://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/air-deccan-launches-2-flightdelhi-dehradun-delhi-sector_229220.html |access-date=7 August 2014 |publisher=MoneyControl.com |date=22 July 2006}}</ref>

The [[Airports Authority of India]] (AAI) suspended flight operations at the airport from March 2007 till the end of the year in order to execute its airport modernisation plan. The runway was extended from 3,500 feet to 7,000 feet and also broadened from 23 metres to 45 metres to enable the landing of narrow-body jets like the [[Boeing 737]] and the [[Airbus A320]]. The erstwhile terminal was built in 2008, a night landing system was installed, a new terminal building and an [[Air Traffic Control]] (ATC) tower were also constructed.<ref>{{cite news |title=Expansion causes flight suspension at Dehradun airport |url=http://www.livemint.com/Politics/VFuk30XNZPkVa1k1YekxGL/Expansion-causes-flight-suspension-at-Dehradun-airport.html |access-date=7 August 2014 |newspaper=[[Live Mint]] |date=26 February 2007}}</ref>

The expansion work was expected to cost {{INRConvert|72|c}} and was to be completed by the end of 2007.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dehradun airport to get Rs 72-cr facelift |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/dehra-dun-airport-to-get-rs-72-cr-facelift-107022301028_1.html |access-date=7 August 2014 |newspaper=[[Business Standard]] |date=23 February 2007}}</ref> However, it took a few months longer, and scheduled flights resumed in March 2008 with Air Deccan re-launching its flights.<ref name="TRB"/> [[Air India]] launched flights from the airport to Delhi on 28 January 2010,<ref>{{cite news |title=Air India launches Delhi-Dehradun flight |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-air-india-launches-delhi-dehradun-flight-1364529 |access-date=7 August 2014 |newspaper=[[Daily News and Analysis]] |date=28 January 2010}}</ref> followed by [[SpiceJet]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite news |title=SpiceJet launches Delhi-Dehradun flights |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-07-19/news/32747550_1_officer-neil-mills-delhi-dehradun-daily-direct-flights |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812235224/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-07-19/news/32747550_1_officer-neil-mills-delhi-dehradun-daily-direct-flights |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 August 2014 |access-date=7 August 2014 |newspaper=[[The Economic Times]] |date=19 July 2012}}</ref>

==Development==
The domestic terminal building at the airport, built in 2008, covered an area of {{cvt|4200|sqm}} and had glass and steel structure with centralised air conditioning and heating, a [[Flight information display system|Flight Information Display System]] (FIDS) and CCTV surveillance systems. The terminal had a peak-hour passenger handling capacity of 150 passengers and annual handling capacity of 122,000. It had 11 check-in counters, an X-ray baggage scanner, three security check booths in the departures section and two baggage claim conveyor belts in the arrivals section. Its adjoining [[airport apron|apron]] can accommodate two Category 'C' type of aircraft.<ref name="PIB"/>

In September 2018, the [[Airports Authority of India]] (AAI) approached the [[Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change]] (MoEFCC) for clearance to expand the airport by constructing a new integrated terminal building and allied facilities at an investment of {{INRConvert|344.75|c}}.<ref>{{cite news |title=AAI seeks various clearances from Environment Ministry for expansion of 5 airports |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/airlines-/-aviation/aai-seeks-various-clearances-from-environment-ministry-for-expansion-of-5-airports/articleshow/65644347.cms |access-date=24 September 2020 |newspaper=[[The Economic Times]] |date= 2 September 2018}}</ref> It would be a new, centrally air-conditioned modular integrated terminal building, to be built on an area of {{cvt|17961|sqm}} and cover a built-up area of {{cvt|30200|sqm}}. The erstwhile terminal was demolished in 2022 to pave way for the new terminal.<ref name= "PFR"/>
[[File:Dehradun Airport Terminal Inside.jpg|thumb|262x262px|Departure/Arrival Area of the new terminal building]]
[[File:Dehradun Airport Terminal.jpg|thumb|262x262px|The former terminal at Dehradun Airport, demolished in 2022]]The new terminal building covers an area of {{cvt|42776|sqm}}, has a concourse, check-in area, security hold and arrival lounge on the ground floor. Offices are accommodated on the mezzanine floor. The departures area has 48 check-in counters, self-check-in kiosks, in-line baggage screening facility among many other facilities and amenities.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dehradun Airport's first phase upgradation to be completed by next month: AAI |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/airlines-/-aviation/dehradun-airports-first-phase-upgradation-to-be-completed-by-next-month-aai/articleshow/78272219.cms |access-date=24 September 2020 |newspaper=[[The Economic Times]] |date= 23 September 2020}}</ref>

===New terminal building===
In order to meet the increasing passenger footfall in the coming years, the airport has received an expansion and full makeover. The cost of the redevelopment project has been done at about {{INRConvert|486|c}}. The [[Airports Authority of India]] (AAI) has modernised the airport in two phases–the first phase of development includes the construction of a new passenger terminal building, built in two parts, along with a utility block, a parking space, a sewage treatment plant, [[rainwater harvesting]] facilities and other ancillary structures.{{cn|date=July 2026}}

The new terminal initially covered an area of {{cvt|12950|sqm}}, was capable of handling 1,800 passengers during peak hours and about 2 million passengers annually, which now increased to an area of {{cvt|42776|sqm}}, an apron capable of handling 20 [[Airbus A320]] and [[Boeing 737]] type aircraft, and is able to handle 3,240 passengers during peak hours and 4.7 million passengers annually, thereby expanding the capacity of the airport by eightfold.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Terminal at Dehradun's Jolly Grant Airport to Become Operational in October|url=https://www.news18.com/news/auto/new-terminal-at-dehraduns-jolly-grant-airport-to-become-operational-in-october-4232378.html|website=www.news18.com|date=22 September 2021 |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref> The new terminal building has a concourse, check-in areas, security hold and arrival lounge on the ground floor, security hold at first floor, and various offices on the mezzanine floor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dehradun Airport all set to get a world-class makeover to handle more passengers|url=https://www.timesnownews.com/business-economy/industry/article/dehradun-airport-all-set-to-get-a-world-class-makeover-to-handle-more-passengers/656952|access-date=29 September 2020|website=www.timesnownews.com|date=23 September 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

It is equipped with 36 check-in counters, which now increased to 48, four conveyor belts, 12 baggage X-ray machines, self-check-in kiosks, in-line baggage screening facilities, retail and commercial spaces covering an area of about {{cvt|7000|sqm}} and a parking space capable of accommodating 500 vehicles.<ref>{{cite web|title=New terminal building of Dehradun's Jolly Grant Airport inaugurated|url=https://www.aninews.in/news/national/general-news/new-terminal-building-of-dehraduns-jolly-grant-airport-inaugurated20211009051413/|website=www.aninews.in|access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>

As per the plan, the second phase of the development work would include shifting of operations from the existing terminal building to the new one, and construction of the remaining portion of the terminal building, by demolishing the erstwhile terminal, along with the integration of all of the services. The first phase of the project was completed and inaugurated by [[Ministry of Civil Aviation (India)|Minister of Civil Aviation]], [[Jyotiraditya Scindia]], on 7 October 2021,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dehradun Airport all set to get a world-class makeover to handle more passengers|url=https://www.timesnownews.com/business-economy/industry/article/dehradun-airport-all-set-to-get-a-world-class-makeover-to-handle-more-passengers/656952|access-date=16 December 2021|website=www.timesnownews.com|date=23 September 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=देहरादून में बन रहा है ये शानदार वर्ल्ड क्लास एयरपोर्ट, तस्वीरों में देखिए भव्यता|url=https://navbharattimes.indiatimes.com/business/business-news/dehradun-airport-gearing-up-for-a-makeover-and-enhanced-capacity/articleshow/78273852.cms|access-date=16 December 2021|website=Navbharat Times|language=hi}}</ref> and the second phase was inaugurated by [[List of Chief Ministers of Uttarakhand|Chief Minister]] [[Pushkar Singh Dhami]] and Jyotiraditya Scindia on 14 February 2024.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dehradun Airport Update: New terminal building of Jolly Grant airport inaugurated; here's all about its capacity and other features|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/airlines-aviation-dehradun-airport-update-new-terminal-building-of-jolly-grant-airport-inaugurated-heres-all-about-its-capacity-and-other-features-3394477/|work=The Financial Express|date=14 February 2024|access-date=15 February 2024|language=en}}</ref>
